beliefs: Outer branch |x|>=2 is sign(x)*A*|x|^p*exp(k*|x|) with A,p,k fit to E1/E2/E7/E8/E10 magnitudes [E1, E2, E7, E8, E10]
Outer branch is odd: f(-x)=-f(x) for |x|>=2, confirmed at moderate and large |x| [E8, E10, E11, E12, E13]
f(2)=-60.2 exactly and f(-2)=-67.0 exactly; the outer law is only approximate near |x|=2 [E1, E4, E6]
On (0,1) f is exactly 0, with a sharp step to -4.3 at x=1.0 [E5, E9]
On (1,2) f rises smoothly from -4.3 toward ~-30 as x->2- [E3, E4, E5, E9]
On (-2,0) f is a smooth curve: ~+6 near -1, peaking ~+8 near -1.2, then dropping steeply to -67 at x=-2 [E3, E6]
Outer branch sign is negative for positive x (f(x)<0 for x>=2), positive for negative x [E1, E2, E7, E8, E10, E11, E12, E13]
The outer law's sign convention: f(x) = -sign(x)*A*|x|^p*exp(k*|x|) (negative on positive side, positive on negative side) [E13]
notes: E13 confirms the outer branch is exactly odd (f(-x)=-f(x)) at moderate |x|. The sign convention in outer() was already correct (negative for positive x, positive for negative x). The remaining mismatch is the magnitude fit A,p,k, which is slightly off (e.g. predicts -124 vs -137 at x=2.5). I refit the log-linear model on the full outer dataset including E13's values to tighten A,p,k.
